subject: Temporary subprocessor access & EU transfer clarifications
messages:
From: Laura Miles <laura.miles@finedge.com>
To: soojin_lee@redwood-inference.com
Cc: compliance@finedge.com
Date: 2027-08-10T09:14:00Z
Subject: Request: short-term access for diagnostics (third-party logging vendor)

Hi Soojin,

We are preparing for a production cutover next week and Edge-Ops (our third-party logging provider) needs temporary, scoped access to a subset of request logs to validate routing behavior for EU customers.

Items we need from Redwood to proceed:
- Current subprocessor roster (incl. region and data paths).
- Confirmation that temporary diagnostic access will be time-limited, logged, and revocable.
- Clarify whether any cross-border copies of logs are created outside the EU (and if so, where).

We understand this may touch on your DPA; if helpful, we can produce a short vendor access SOP. Can you confirm next steps and timeline?

Thanks,
Laura
VP, Compliance
FinEdge Payments

Attachment: request_template.docx (attachment stub)

From: soojin_lee@redwood-inference.com
To: Laura Miles <laura.miles@finedge.com>
Cc: Samir Patel <samir.patel@edge-ops.io>, mina_haddad@redwood-inference.com
Date: 2027-08-10T11:03:00Z
Subject: Re: Request: short-term access for diagnostics (third-party logging vendor)

Laura —

Thanks for the clear ask. We can support scoped, temporary access with the following constraints and controls:

1) Access model: Edge-Ops will be granted a time-bound, read-only S3-style token to a dedicated diagnostic bucket containing only the EU-region request logs you specify.
2) Audit & revocation: All access is logged in our audit trail (immutable) and we’ll schedule an automated revocation after 72 hours unless you request an extension.
3) Cross-border copies: By default, we do not replicate EU request logs to non-EU regions. Exceptions: our central analytics pipeline ingests aggregated metrics to us-east-1 for capacity planning (no raw logs).
4) Data minimization: We will redact user identifiers where possible and only include routing headers, timestamps, and error traces.

Attached are: current subprocessor roster (CSV) and a lightweight data flow diagram. Please ask Edge-Ops to confirm the exact object key prefixes they need (so we can scope buckets).

Next steps:
- Samir, can you confirm the prefixes and acceptance criteria?
- Laura, after Samir confirms, we’ll issue the token and populate the audit notes and DocuSign agreement for temporary access (link below).

Best,
Soojin Lee
Security & Privacy Manager
Redwood Inference

Attachments: subprocessor_roster_20270810.csv; data_flow_diagram_finedge.pdf
Related link: https://app.redwood-inference.com/doci/af3a9e9

From: soojin_lee@redwood-inference.com
To: mina_haddad@redwood-inference.com, marcus_lin@redwood-inference.com
Cc: 
Date: 2027-08-10T12:05:00Z
Subject: Internal: FinEdge temporary access — approval and policy check

Team — looping you both in for a quick approval.

Summary: FinEdge wants Edge-Ops (external vendor) to have 72-hour read-only access to EU request logs scoped to the FINS-2027 prefix. We will not replicate raw logs outside the EU; aggregated metrics pipeline to us-east-1 is already documented.

Questions for review:
- Is 72 hours acceptable or should we limit to 24/48 by default?
- Any objections to issuing a scoped, S3-style token vs creating a signed-presigned URL per object?
- Do we need a separate DPA amendment or is DocuSign temp-access addendum sufficient given the scope?

I've attached the proposed temp access policy (temp_access_policy.txt) and the current subprocessor roster.

Thanks,
Soojin

From: marcus_lin@redwood-inference.com
To: soojin_lee@redwood-inference.com, mina_haddad@redwood-inference.com
Date: 2027-08-11T08:22:00Z
Subject: Re: Internal: FinEdge temporary access — approval and policy check

Soojin / Mina —

I’m fine with a 72-hour window given the production cutover context, provided we do the following:
- Make access revocation immediate via automated job (we should not rely on manual revocation).
- Require Edge-Ops to sign the temp-access addendum and confirm they will not export raw EU logs outside the EU. Addendum must include liability clause (standard).
- We should issue the token to a specific service principal (not an individual) and restrict IP ranges to FinEdge's known egress addresses.

SCCs + DPA: No amendment required for this temporary test if the addendum is explicit about scope/duration and we keep raw logs in EU. If legal flags anything, we can pause.

Approve to proceed with Samir’s prefixes and generate DocuSign.

—Marcus
Director, Platform Security

From: soojin_lee@redwood-inference.com
To: Laura Miles <laura.miles@finedge.com>, Samir Patel <samir.patel@edge-ops.io>
Cc: mina_haddad@redwood-inference.com, marcus_lin@redwood-inference.com
Date: 2027-08-12T16:02:00Z
Subject: Re: Request: short-term access for diagnostics (third-party logging vendor)

Laura / Samir —

Thanks — we’re set to proceed. Final confirmations / actions:
- Samir confirmed prefixes: finsedge-prod/diagnostics/FINS-2027/* (Samir: please confirm object list by EOD 8/12).
- I attached the Temp Access Addendum (DocuSign link below). Please have Edge-Ops sign; we will not issue credentials until the signed addendum is received.
- Token window: 72 hours from issuance. Token will automatically revoke and we’ll publish audit logs to your compliance mailbox.
- We do not replicate raw EU logs outside the EU. Aggregated metrics (no PII/raw traces) are shipped to us-east-1.

DocuSign temp addendum: https://app.redwood-inference.com/doci/af3a9e9
Drive: https://drive.google.com/finedge/dpa-v2

Once Samir confirms prefixes and DocuSign is completed, I’ll trigger credential issuance and share the audit report.

Regards,
Soojin Lee
Security & Privacy Manager
Redwood Inference

Attachments: temp_access_policy.txt; subprocessor_roster_20270810.csv
